_what: The numbers and names tools/publish-an-engine-release uses. `signing_domain` is the first line of the text each release's Ed25519 signature covers (the engine's release-feed reader, engine job J1, checks the same text). `keep_releases` is how many entries feed.json holds at most; an older entry leaves with its tar.gz. `binary` is the engine program cargo builds and the tar.gz holds beside the repository's `product_folder`. `feed_file` is the feed's name in the feed folder. `commit_pattern` and `target_pattern` are the only commit ids and rust target triples a path is made from. `urgent_trailer` is the commit-message trailer that marks a release urgent (`Release-Urgent: true`). `key_file_mode` is the signing key file's mode (0400); a key file anyone else can read is refused. `private_input_bytes_at_most` bounds what descriptors 3 and 4 may hold. `push_body_bytes_at_most` bounds one push delivery (GitHub caps a delivery at 25 MB). `build_timeout_ms` and `git_timeout_ms` bound one build and one git call. `on_builder` is where install puts everything on the builder: the system user that builds and signs, its work folder, the feed folder Caddy serves, the signing key, the SSH key git reads a repository named by an ssh:// or git@ URL with (made on the builder; its public half is answered, to add to the repository as a read-only deploy key) and that SSH connection's known hosts, the tool's own files, the config, the receiver's state, and the encrypted credentials. `feed_path` is where Caddy serves the feed folder under the builder's name; `push_path` is where GitHub sends push deliveries; `receiver_port` is the receiver's port on 127.0.0.1. `node_major_at_least` is the Node.js the builder needs (the content identity's BLAKE3 module needs 20.19 or later); `node_dist` is where install fetches it when the builder has none, checked against that folder's SHASUMS256.txt. `rustup_url` installs the rust toolchain for the builder user when it has no cargo; the repository's own rust-toolchain file then picks the version.
